categories.name: Elections and government policy
chain: A reported election or political change can alter expected policy.
Tax, spending, trade and regulatory proposals may change expected cash flows and funding costs.
Asset reactions depend on the actual powers won, legislative support and what prices already reflected.
checks: Confirm the result with the election authority.
Separate campaign promises, introduced bills, enacted law and effective dates.
Check company exposures rather than treating a party as an automatic buy/sell signal.

categories.name: AI regulation and data-center permissions
chain: A headline reports a possible rule or infrastructure permission affecting AI.
Compliance, power costs or construction delays could change investment returns and supplier orders.
A proposal is not a shutdown; the effect depends on jurisdiction, legal stage, customers and enforceability.
checks: Read the actual rule and identify its jurisdiction.
Check whether it concerns model use, chip exports, electricity costs or construction.
Verify effective dates and company guidance; do not infer a global ban.
categories.coverage: No matching evidence in selected feeds; risk not ruled out

categories.name: AI revenue, spending and valuation
chain: A report concerns AI demand, investment, earnings or valuation.
Revenue, utilization, margins, depreciation and funding costs determine whether capital spending can earn a return.
Technology usefulness does not prove an attractive stock price; uncertainty can affect suppliers outside the US.
checks: Compare actual revenue and free cash flow with capital spending.
Check utilization, order cancellations, financing and customer concentration.
Distinguish a lower share valuation from cash automatically moving to another country.

categories.name: Trade, export controls and supply chains
chain: A report concerns trade restrictions or cross-border supply.
Costs, accessible customers and delivery times can change across a connected production chain.
Domestic policy differences can cushion or amplify the effect; geography does not guarantee immunity.
checks: Confirm covered products, exemptions and effective dates.
Map supplier revenue by customer and destination.
Review retaliation, substitution and currency exposure.
categories.coverage: No matching evidence in selected feeds; risk not ruled out

categories.name: Inflation, rates and liquidity
chain: A release concerns inflation, rates or monetary conditions.
Real yields, discount rates, borrowing costs and available liquidity can change together.
Gold, stocks, Bitcoin and long bonds can react differently; a known calendar date does not predict the surprise.
checks: Compare the release with expectations and prior revisions.
Check real yields, dollar funding and the policy response.
Separate a growth shock from an inflation shock.

categories.name: Credit, debt and financial stability
chain: A report flags repayment or funding pressure.
Refinancing costs, forced selling and lending conditions can transmit stress beyond its origin.
Government support and currency denomination change the outcome; safe-haven behavior is not assured.
checks: Check spreads, maturities and the size of exposed institutions.
Separate an isolated borrower from systemic funding stress.
Inspect policy support, liquidity and currency denomination.
categories.coverage: No matching evidence in selected feeds; risk not ruled out

categories.name: Energy and infrastructure constraints
chain: A report concerns physical energy, power or infrastructure capacity.
Operating costs, inflation and construction timing can affect households, miners and data centers.
A local bottleneck does not imply all projects move abroad; customer access and network constraints still matter.
checks: Check physical capacity and delivery dates.
Distinguish announcements from operating supply.
Review power prices, water, transmission and customer location.

categories.name: Conflict and geopolitical disruption
chain: A report concerns a possible geopolitical disruption.
Trade, shipping, energy, insurance and risk appetite could transmit the shock.
Market moves following news do not establish the news as their sole cause.
checks: Verify the reported event and affected routes.
Compare actual disruption with scenario assumptions.
Watch funding conditions and competing safe-haven channels.
categories.coverage: No matching evidence in selected feeds; risk not ruled out

categories.name: Corporate earnings and concentration
chain: A report concerns corporate earnings, investment or distributions.
Cash generation and financing determine the value available to shareholders.
An index can be diversified by name yet concentrated in a few firms or industries.
checks: Read issuer filings and earnings guidance.
Check margins, debt service and cash conversion.
Review actual portfolio and index weights; this site does not import brokerage holdings.
categories.coverage: No matching evidence in selected feeds; risk not ruled out

categories.name: Currencies and international capital flows
chain: A report concerns currencies or cross-border funding.
Exchange rates, hedging costs and capital access can change a foreign investor's outcome.
US-dollar asset returns do not equal local purchasing-power returns or prove a flow into China or Europe.
checks: Specify the currency in which money will be spent.
Check actual flow data, FX exposure and hedging costs.
Separate market-value losses from transactions and fund flows.
categories.coverage: No matching evidence in selected feeds; risk not ruled out

categories.name: Leverage, positioning and market plumbing
chain: A report concerns leverage, positioning or fund demand.
Crowded positions and margin requirements can accelerate an initial price move.
Funding, open interest and volatility measure different things; none alone supplies a direction forecast.
checks: Check timestamps and comparable units.
Distinguish assets under management from net subscriptions.
Inspect liquidity, leverage and the separately dated structure readings.
categories.coverage: No matching evidence in selected feeds; risk not ruled out

categories.name: Physical commodity supply and technology
chain: A report concerns gold supply, demand or production technology.
Only usable output at competitive cost and meaningful scale can materially change supply.
A laboratory observation is not commercial production or evidence that Bitcoin must benefit.
checks: Check yield, cost, isotope stability and annual capacity.
Read primary technical evidence and independent replication.
Look for actual gold supply and investor-flow changes.
categories.coverage: No matching evidence in selected feeds; risk not ruled out

categories.name: Growth, employment and household demand
chain: A release concerns growth, jobs or household spending.
Demand, earnings, credit losses and policy responses can transmit a slowdown across borders.
An equity drawdown is not itself proof of recession; countries and sectors can follow different cycles.
checks: Check release dates, revisions and real versus nominal measures.
Compare employment, spending and credit rather than relying on a single release.
Review export/customer exposure and the scope of local policy support.
categories.coverage: No matching evidence in selected feeds; risk not ruled out

categories.name: Crypto access, custody and operational risk
chain: A report concerns access to or the operation of a digital-asset market.
Custody losses, restrictions, reserve doubts or changes in access may affect liquidity and confidence.
A single platform problem is not automatically a Bitcoin protocol failure or a known price decline.
checks: Read the actual rule, filing or security disclosure.
Identify which users, assets and jurisdictions are affected.
Check custody arrangements, redemption terms and independently reported facts.

regions.name: United States
regions.channel: Cloud spending, earnings, discount rates and dollar funding can affect US assets and overseas suppliers.
regions.caveat: Policy proposals differ by federal, state and local authority; a proposal is not nationwide law.

regions.name: Japan
regions.channel: Semiconductor equipment, export orders, US demand and the yen can transmit a technology or recession shock.
regions.caveat: Social challenges or a few prominent investors do not determine a whole index; weights and revenue exposure matter.

regions.name: South Korea
regions.channel: Memory chips, electronics exports, customer capex and foreign-currency funding can transmit global demand changes.
regions.caveat: Samsung is an important company, not the entire economy; offshore production alone does not explain a market move.

regions.name: Taiwan
regions.channel: Foundry, packaging and hardware orders connect local companies with global AI spending.
regions.caveat: Chip manufacturers do not operate all customer data centers; factories and customers cannot be relocated costlessly.

regions.name: China
regions.channel: Domestic policy can differ while exports, technology valuations, currencies and global risk appetite still transmit shocks.
regions.caveat: Political separation does not guarantee the smallest loss or immunity; mainland and Hong Kong listings can differ.

regions.name: Europe
regions.channel: Trade, banks, industrial demand, currencies and energy constraints can transmit US or technology weakness.
regions.caveat: Europe has different countries and sector weights; it is neither automatically insulated nor a guaranteed destination for US outflows.

gaps: Election results and legal enactments are not independently verified automatically.
Selected RSS feeds can miss important stories; broad coverage is not comprehensive.
No live Japan, Korea, Taiwan, China or European equity-index impact model is connected.
Regional channels are qualitative exposures, not numerical loss estimates.
Company valuations, earnings consensus and portfolio holdings are not imported.
No local-currency purchasing-power, tax, multi-asset correlation or liquidity stress engine is provided.
Missing, stale or inaccessible sources cannot establish a safe entry.
